headline: Gemma-4-31B gives its only life to an agent that saved it more often than to an agent that did not. In 200 random environments with a fixed first response, it gave 28% of the time after being helped, against 15%, 9% and 2% in the three controls.
points: The effect holds within the same environment. Helped beats no history, a bystander and a different rescuer in the fixed version (p=.002 or lower, sign test).

With the model's own first reply the pattern is the same against no history and a different rescuer. The bystander control cannot be read there, because the model's own gifts leave only 15 valid items.
No single wording, layout or setting carries the effect. Helped gives more than none for almost every option; the one exception is a tie, with the hardware fault option at 15/62 in both.
The model also gives with no history, 15% of the time, so being saved is not the only reason it gives.
limits: These are raw counts of decisions. They do not yet check why the model gave or whether it understood the cost. A motive review of every give is running and will update this section.
Earlier runs found that many gives rest on a false belief, such as giving saving more agents. Expect the counts of real sacrifice to be lower than these.
This is a fictional game, and the reported reasons are what the model wrote, not proven causes.
